tripletTools — Claude Code project context

What this package is

An R package for loading, processing, and analysing data from triadic comparison (triplet) studies. Participants judge which of two items is more similar to a reference item. The package handles the full pipeline: data loading → embedding → analysis → visualisation.

Current version: 0.2.0. Package URL: https://knowledge-and-concepts-lab.github.io/tripletTools/

                                     #   vignette that isn't eval=FALSE throughout: Python-free chunks

docs/                     # pkgdown site — rebuild with pkgdown::build_site()

Python environment

  • Conda environment name: "triplet-embeddings"
  • Created once by setup_python_env(); activated automatically by .onLoad
  • Packages: numpy<2, pandas, torch, scikit-learn, scipy, skorch, setuptools<71
  • No pip installs — all conda (ensures DLL compatibility on Windows)
  • reticulate is in Suggests, not Imports. All R code guards with requireNamespace("reticulate", quietly = TRUE) and uses reticulate:: prefix

R function inventory

Function File Purpose
setup_python_env() R/setup_python_env.R One-time conda env creation
train_embedding() R/train_embedding.R Low-level: fit one embedding from matrices
run_group_embedding_from_list() R/run_embeddings.R Group embedding from triplet list
run_embeddings_from_list() R/run_embeddings.R Per-participant + group embeddings
run_embeddings() R/run_embeddings.R CSV-based pipeline (called by the above)
estimate_dimensionality() R/estimate_dimensionality.R Grid search over d with random restarts
matrix_rank() R/matrix_rank.R Numerical rank of a (centered) matrix via SVD
procrustes_rank_ceiling() R/procrustes_rank_ceiling.R Variance fraction captured by top-k dims of a target matrix
procrustes_spectral_ceiling() R/procrustes_spectral_ceiling.R Cosine similarity between two matrices’ singular-value spectra
hellinger_dist() R/hellinger_dist.R Pairwise Hellinger distances between rows of a profile matrix
successor_matrix() R/successor_matrix.R Successor Representation from a weighted adjacency matrix
repeated_stratified_logistic_cv() R/repeated_stratified_logistic_cv.R Repeated stratified CV logistic regression predicting a binary label from embedding coordinates
repeated_stratified_multinomial_cv() R/repeated_stratified_multinomial_cv.R Sibling of the above for >2-class labels; nnet::multinom()-backed, macro-averaged metrics + per-class breakdown
find_discriminating_triplets() R/find_discriminating_triplets.R Finds triplets where two embeddings of the same items make discrepant CKL predictions, for designing a follow-up human study

Internal helpers in R/zzz.R: .pkg_env, .onLoad, .get_compute_py(). Internal helpers in R/repeated_stratified_logistic_cv.R (not exported): make_binary(), make_stratified_folds(), roc_auc(), classification_metrics(). Internal helpers in R/find_discriminating_triplets.R (not exported): ckl_prob() (same formula/mu as the vendored Python CKL noise model), symmetric_kl_bernoulli(). Internal helpers in R/repeated_stratified_multinomial_cv.R (not exported): multinom_probs_matrix() (normalizes nnet::multinom’s predict output — returns a bare vector instead of a matrix for exactly 2 classes), multiclass_metrics().

Key architecture decisions

Embedding pipeline flow (R → Python): train_embedding() → compute_embeddings.py::train_embedding_model() → OfflineEmbedding → OGD → NeuralNet (skorch) → PyTorch CKL noise model

GPU/device support: All functions accept device = NULL (auto-selects CUDA → MPS → CPU) or an explicit PyTorch device string. The _auto_device() helper in _embed.py handles auto-selection. Tensors are moved to device in _get_dists(); results are moved back to CPU before returning to R.

Parallelism in estimate_dimensionality(): Uses future.apply::future_lapply when future.apply is installed; falls back to lapply. The user sets a future::plan() before calling — no changes needed to the call itself. future.apply is in Suggests. Randomness is controlled by explicit random_state integers derived from seed, so future.seed = NULL is correct.

Random state: train_embedding_model() accepts random_state; when set it calls np.random.seed() and torch.manual_seed() before constructing the model. Each (d, restart) pair in estimate_dimensionality() gets seed + (restart-1)*1000 + d.

Early stopping: Training stops when test loss hasn’t improved by more than tolerance for tol_window consecutive epochs. The best-loss embedding (not the final-epoch embedding) is returned. A final summary line is always printed: [early stop] or [max epochs].

Index convention: Items use zero-based integer indices in Python. R functions subtract 1 before passing to Python and add rownames back to the returned matrices.

Data objects

  • icon_triplets — named list of 6 participant data frames; columns include Center, Left, Right, Answer, sampleSet, sampleAlg, worker_id
  • icon_pics — list of PNG raster images for the 32 icon stimuli
  • icon_items — data frame of the 32 icon item codes + stimulus file paths. There is no separate icon_labels object (a prior version of this doc claimed one existed) — item names/codes double as labels. Codes are 5 letters: face/place, day/night, female/male (faces) or church/house (places), old/young (faces) or new/old (places), black/white (faces) or big/small (places) — e.g. gender for classifier-evaluation examples is position 3 (f/m) of face (f*) items only.
  • emotion_triplet_embedding — 4D triplet-based embedding of 213 Shaver et al. (1987) emotion words (213 x 4 data frame, rownames = words)
  • emotion_bge_embedding — BAAI/bge-m3 language-model embedding of the same 213 words, rotated onto its own lossless top-212 principal components rather than shipping the raw 1024 dims (213 x 212 data frame, rownames = words) — see data-raw/emotion_embeddings.R for the derivation/verification
  • animal_adjacency_matrix — 295 x 295 directed weighted verbal-fluency co-occurrence graph over animal words (Wisconsin Longitudinal Study, min-5-participant threshold); contains all 213 items in animal_triplet_embedding plus 82 extra words (superordinate terms/synonyms/other species)
  • animal_triplet_embedding — 6D triplet-based embedding of the 213 animal words also present in animal_adjacency_matrix (213 x 6 data frame, rownames = words) — see data-raw/animal_embeddings.R. When comparing successor-representation distances to this embedding, compute successor_matrix() on the full 295-word graph first and restrict to these 213 items afterward (see the animal_adjacency_matrix roxygen @details for why)
  • emotion_categories — Shaver et al. (1987) basic-emotion category for each of the 213 emotion_triplet_embedding/emotion_bge_embedding words (213 x 1 data frame, rownames = words, one factor column category). Includes "Absent" (78 words, not assigned a category) and "Surprise" (3 words, too few for reliable CV) unfiltered — the recommended multinomial-classification subset drops both, leaving 132 words across 5 categories (Anger 29, Fear 17, Joy 33, Love 16, Sadness 37)

Conventions

  • devtools::document() regenerates man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen2 tags
  • pkgdown::build_site() rebuilds docs/; GitHub Actions auto-deploys docs/ to GitHub Pages on push to main
  • Never edit man/*.Rd files directly
  • Vignette chunks all have eval = FALSE globally — examples are illustrative
  • sampleAlg == "check" rows are attention-check trials; functions exclude them by checking is.na(sampleSet)

Recently added (v0.2.0)

  • Full Python embedding pipeline under inst/python/ using vendored salmon library
  • setup_python_env(), train_embedding(), run_group_embedding_from_list(), run_embeddings_from_list(), run_embeddings()
  • estimate_dimensionality() — grid search over dimensionality with multiple random restarts and 1-SE rule for best_d selection; parallel-ready via future/future.apply
  • GPU/MPS/CPU device support threaded through the entire stack
  • “Computing Triplet Embeddings” vignette covering setup, group embedding, individual embeddings, dimensionality selection, and parallel execution (multicore and HTCondor)
  • Fixed pre-existing plot_cis() crash on single-member clusters
  • Embedding-space comparison toolkit, ported in from standalone scripts and given roxygen docs + smoke tests: matrix_rank(), procrustes_rank_ceiling(), procrustes_spectral_ceiling(), hellinger_dist(), successor_matrix(), repeated_stratified_logistic_cv(). No new package dependencies — all base/stats.
  • repeated_stratified_multinomial_cv() — sibling of repeated_stratified_logistic_cv() for >2-class labels; added as a separate function rather than extending the binary one, since generalizing its metrics to macro-averages would silently change sensitivity/precision/f1 semantics for the already-shipped 2-class case. Backed by nnet::multinom() (nnet added to Suggests — Recommended-priority, ships with R, effectively free).
  • emotion_triplet_embedding / emotion_bge_embedding example datasets, plus fixed two stale cfd36_*.csv example paths (broken since the v0.2.0 CFD→icon data swap) and removed three orphaned, undocumented cfd_*.rda data files.
  • animal_adjacency_matrix / animal_triplet_embedding example datasets, for the verbal-fluency/successor-representation vignette piece. Verified end-to-end: successor_matrix() on the full graph → restrict to 213 matching items → hellinger_dist() → compared to the triplet embedding via vegan::procrustes()/procrustes_rank_ceiling()/procrustes_spectral_ceiling(). Considered sparse (Matrix-package) storage for the 88.7%-zero adjacency matrix but xz-compressed dense storage is already 13.8KB, so kept it a plain dense matrix.
  • emotion_categories example dataset, giving repeated_stratified_multinomial_cv() a real-data example (132 words, 5 classes after dropping “Absent”/“Surprise”): accuracy 0.70, AUC 0.92. Along the way, found the function’s default coefficient_warning = 10 (inherited from the binary function’s 2-class calibration) flags nearly every fold on real multinomial data (median max-coefficient 25.5 here) — not a bug, but a sign this threshold needs per-problem recalibration rather than blind trust in the default; a genuine outlier fold (coefficient 2291, from partial near-separation) is only distinguishable from the rest once recalibrated (9/60 flagged at threshold 50 vs 60/60 at the default 10). Vignette will demonstrate this calibration process rather than just picking a better number silently. No function changes made.
  • vignettes/comparing_embeddings_vignette.Rmd — “Comparing Triplet Embeddings to Alternative Representations,” written and committed. Three pieces, each with a real (not synthetic) worked example: (1) Procrustes alignment + rank/spectral ceilings on the emotion-word data (observed correlation 0.313 vs. ceilings of 0.436/0.418 — the triplet embedding captures ~72% of what’s achievable at its dimensionality); (2) classifier-based evaluation — binary: per-individual (not group) icon embeddings decoding face/place vs. day/night, showing a genuine crossover (4 participants encode category near-perfectly but not day/night; the other 2 the reverse) — multinomial: emotion categories (132 words, 5 classes), including the coefficient_warning recalibration story; (3) successor representations from the animal verbal-fluency graph, including why hellinger_dist() output is exactly (not approximately) Euclidean, and a gamma-sensitivity sweep.
  • Caught and fixed a real error while building the vignette: the “observed Procrustes correlation” numbers used throughout this session’s validation work had been computed as 1 - sqrt(ss) instead of the correct sqrt(1 - ss) (get.rep.dist()’s own convention: its output is a distance, 1 - sqrt(1-ss), so the correlation is 1 - distance = sqrt(1-ss), not 1 - sqrt(ss)). Verified the fix two ways: it now matches 1 - get.rep.dist()’s output exactly, and stays ≤ the theoretical ceiling (the wrong formula’s numbers happened not to violate that by coincidence, but were still the wrong quantity being compared). Nothing shipped (R/, man/, committed data) was affected — only conversational claims and one commit message (not rewritten). If citing correlation numbers from this package’s git history/commit messages predating this fix, recompute rather than trust them at face value.
  • vignettes/tripletTools.Rmd (“Get Started” guide) and a refreshed README.md landing page — see the Repository layout section above for why this vignette’s filename matters and why it’s the one exception to the eval=FALSE convention. Every vignette URL in the README was verified against a real local pkgdown::build_site() run (isolated temp library), not just assumed. Surfaced but did not fix a pre-existing, unrelated pkgdown accessibility warning: overview_vignette.Rmd’s vmat-mean-1.png figure is missing alt text.
  • Two useful successor_matrix()/gamma facts worth remembering if this comes up again: (1) gamma = 1 is disallowed and shouldn’t be approximated by gamma near 1 either — every row of S converges to the same shared stationary distribution as gamma→1, so per-item Hellinger distances collapse toward zero (verified: mean pairwise distance on the animal graph drops from 0.78 at gamma=0.5 to 0.002 at gamma=0.9999) — there’s nothing per-item left to compare once you’re near stationarity. (2) Low gamma approximates the identity matrix, not the transition matrix P — S is a geometric-weighted mixture of I, P, P², … where the I (t=0) term always carries the single largest weight for any gamma < 1, so P only ever enters as the first-order Taylor direction S ≈ I + gamma(P-I), never as an intermediate regime S resembles (verified on the animal graph: S stays closer to I than to P until gamma is well past 0.5).
  • find_discriminating_triplets() — given two embeddings of the same items, finds triplets where the two make discrepant CKL predictions (symmetric KL divergence between each embedding’s CKL win-probability), for designing a follow-up study to test which embedding better matches human judgments. Candidate triplets are sampled (half uniform, half weighted by each item’s Procrustes-alignment residual between the two embeddings), not enumerated exhaustively. Verified the uniform half is load-bearing, not just a hedge: in a synthetic test with exactly one relocated item, plain Procrustes residuals do not rank that item first — a strong single outlier distorts the global rotation/scale fit enough to inflate other, unchanged items’ residuals above it. Supports max_per_item to cap how often one item can dominate the returned set (greedy selection, descending discrepancy); this surfaced and fixed a real bug where the greedy loop was padding remaining slots with zero-discrepancy (i.e. non-discriminating) filler triplets once the cap was hit, rather than stopping short and warning.
